bills.summary: This bill would reduce Georgia's income-tax rate. The official text also sets when the change applies and repeals conflicting law.

bills.title: Second Amendment Preservation Act; enact
bills.summary: This bill, titled the Second Amendment Preservation Act, would add protections it describes as guarding the right to keep and bear arms. It would also prohibit public officers and employees from enforcing, or helping to enforce, certain federal gun laws or actions.
bills.officialSummary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to amend Article 4 of Chapter 11 of Title 16 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to dangerous instrumentalities and practices, so as to provide for protections against the infringements on the right to keep and bear arms; to provide for a short title; to provide for legislative findings and intent; to provide for definitions; to prohibit public officers or employees from enforcing or providing assistance for the enforcement of federal laws or actions
bills.watchNote: Opinion: Sponsors present this as a Second Amendment bill. Whether a state can limit help with federal gun enforcement is a legal fight this page does not decide.

bills.title: Local government; procedures for real property owners to make claims for compensation for loss of property value or expenses incurred; provisions
bills.summary: This bill would create a procedure for real property owners to claim compensation from a local government for lost property value or expenses when that government fails to follow or enforce certain laws, ordinances, or resolutions. The compiled official summary is cut off mid-sentence; the legislature's page has the full text.
bills.officialSummary: A BILL to be entitled an Act to amend Chapter 60 of Title 36 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to general provisions applicable to counties and municipal corporations, so as to provide procedures for real property owners to make claims for compensation from local governments for loss of property value or expenses incurred due to the local government's failure to comply with or nonenforcement of certain laws, ordinances, and resolutions or due to the local government maintaining
bills.watchNote: Opinion: This is a property-rights bill about payment when local government inaction costs an owner. Who qualifies is a legal question, not something this page decides.
